chunks: And by this chain, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from Yunus, from Jahm ibn Abi Jahma, from the one who narrated to him, from Abu 'Abdillah (Imam al-Sadiq), peace be upon him — he said:

'Verily, Allah azwj Mighty and Majestic informed Muhammad saww of whatever had existed since the coming into being of the world, and of whatever would occur until the expiry of the world, and informed him of the Ordained (mahtum) matters from that, and He made an exception upon him regarding what was besides it.'

key_terms.اسْتَثْنَى: He made an exception/excluded — God retained the ability to alter what is not Mahtum, a foundation of the Bada' doctrine
key_terms.الْمَحْتُومِ: the Ordained — matters irrevocably and definitively decreed by God, not subject to Bada' (alteration of decree)
key_terms.انْقِضَاءِ: expiry, termination — the end/destruction of the world

ai.seo_question: What distinction did Allah make between ordained (mahtum) and non-ordained matters when informing the Prophet of all past and future events, according to Imam al-Sadiq in al-Kafi?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) reports that Allah disclosed to the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) all events from the world's beginning to its end. Crucially, this disclosure distinguished al-Mahtum — irrevocably and definitively decreed matters — from other matters, for which Allah retained the capacity to alter His decree. This distinction is the theological core of the doctrine of al-Bada' (apparent alteration of divine will), the very chapter topic in al-Kafi within which this hadith appears.

en.hubeali:
And by this chain, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ja’far Bin Muhammad, from Yunus, from Jahm Bin Abu Jahma, from the one who narrated it, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Informed Muhammad<sup>saww</sup> with whatever had happened since the coming into being of the world, and with whatever was going to happen up to the expiry of the world, and Informed him<sup>saww</sup> with the Ordained (matters) from that, and Excluded upon him<sup>saww</sup> with regards to what was besides it’.
en.sarwar: 14. It is narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from al-Rayyan ibn al-Salt who has said the following. “I heard Imam al-Rida (a.s.) saying, “
Allah never sent a prophet without the law that prohibits the use of wine and without belief in al-Bada.’”
